about: Every INDSPG variable sorted into input / optimisation / fixed / dependent. 'cad_variables' are the 210 variables INDSPG writes to CADs/INDSPG/indspg_equations_onshape.txt (and the same names to indspg_equations.txt), in that order, under the stage prefixes a1_ / a2_; 43 of them are written twice under both prefixes, and the second name is marked 'alias_of' the first (same value, same classification). 'code_only' are values the code uses but does not write to the CAD file, plus every config key the CAD does not use; 'unused_config_blocks' are config blocks INDSPG never reads. tests/test_variable_categories.py checks the lists against the code and re-evaluates every formula and lookup; docs/variables/idspg.md is generated from this file (python tools/variables/render.py).

categories.input: chosen parts and material: the motor's dimensions and torque, the motor driver's mount dimensions, the gear material's allowable stress
categories.optimisation: searched by the optimiser: teeth, module, number of planets
categories.fixed: constants that don't depend on the design: clearances, wall thicknesses, fastener and bearing choices, feature sizes, the gear standard
categories.dependent: computed from the variables above, by a formula, a catalogue lookup (bearings, bolts, nuts) or a rule the code applies (the tooth-stress rule for face widths)

confidence.high: the code reads it directly from one source, or computes it with an explicit formula
confidence.medium: the code is clear, but the category is a judgement call (see the reason)
confidence.low: can't be decided from the code alone

code_only.reason: motor torque the gears are sized for (peak torque under the default rating setting); sets the face widths

code_only.name: gear_allowable_stress
code_only.reason: allowable tooth stress of the gear material, chosen with the material mode (3dp: PLA, metal: steel); sets the face widths

code_only.name: FOS
code_only.reason: factor of safety in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: serviceFactor
code_only.reason: service factor on the motor torque in the tooth-stress rule

code_only.name: planet_bearing_gap
code_only.reason: axial gap between the two planet bearings (one in each planet gear); with the bearing width it sets the smallest planet and ring width of both stages; one key for both stages, the plan leaves open whether it should be one per stage (planet_bearing_gap1 / 2)

code_only.name: sun_hub_rotor_gap
code_only.reason: extra radial gap between the stage-1 sun hub and the rotor bore, on top of one clearance (2 mm)

code_only.name: rotor_mount_hole_wall
code_only.reason: wall on each side of the rotor mount holes' countersink, which sets the mount-hole circle (2 mm)

code_only.name: sun1_extra_clearance_multiple
code_only.reason: extra stage-1 sun length for this motor, in multiples of standard_clearance_1_5mm (one value per motor: RI100 0, RI80 0.5; replaces a rotor-height == 19 check)

code_only.name: max_diameter_stage1_clearance_multiple
code_only.reason: margin inside the rotor bore for the largest stage-1 diameter, in multiples of standard_clearance_1_5mm (4; read by gearbox_runner)

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter
code_only.reason: largest gearbox diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter): the stator wire's outer diameter less two ring walls, times a factor

code_only.name: maxGearboxDiameter_Stg1
code_only.reason: largest stage-1 diameter the optimiser may use (gearbox_runner max_diameter_stage1): the rotor's inner diameter less max_diameter_stage1_clearance_multiple x standard_clearance_1_5mm

code_only.name: a1_sun_bottom_casing_bearing_massKg
code_only.reason: a two-case value: when the rotor is 19 mm high (RI80) the bearing is the catalogue one for the rotor's bore, otherwise (RI100) the config value a1_sun_bottom_casing_bearing_massKg; catalogue bearing chosen by bearings_discrete for the bore the stage needs (smallest one that fits); this is its mass
